signals.signal: regional. Mellon Technologies' 2025 group accounts, reported 11/08/2026, give the first verifiable Mellon scale figures and correct the prior 'unverifiable/conflicting' baseline: group revenue EUR 258.82m (2024: EUR 220.7m, +17%), EBITDA EUR 14.13m, net profit EUR 6.83m (2024: EUR 3.9m), presence in >12 countries and >9,600 staff, with management guiding to further growth in 2026. In 2025 Mellon entered TWO new Printec footprint countries by incorporating wholly-owned subsidiaries Mellon Systems and Services d.o.o. (Ljubljana, Slovenia) and Mellon Hungary LLC (Budapest, Hungary). Neither appears yet on Mellon's own public company list (which shows only Albania incl. a Kosovo branch, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Ukraine plus the Greek entities), so these are pre-launch entities. The same report restates the National Bank of Greece ATM-network modernisation on Korean Hyosung machines plus KAL ATM-management software.
signals.source_name: mononews.gr - 'Mellon Technologies: Nea epektasi se Slovenia - Oungaria kai tziros EUR 259 ekat. to 2025' (corroborated by mellongroup.com/companies)
signals.implies: Printec's closest regional rival is now a EUR 259m-revenue group and has just planted legal entities in Slovenia and Hungary, two markets Printec already sells into (Printec S.I. d.o.o. holds the Posta Slovenije parcel-locker contract). Mellon's standard bundle - Hyosung ATMs and recyclers, KAL multivendor ATM software, Ingenico POS with managed services, and queue-management branch kit - lines up almost exactly against Printec's NCR ATM line, x-core multivendor software, Verifone/Castles POS with TMS, and managed/field services. Printec should lock multi-year managed-service and software renewals with its Slovenian and Hungarian accounts now, before Mellon's local entities are staffed and start bidding.
signals.likelihood: First Mellon SI/HU commercial approaches within 6-12 months; a named bank win less certain in that window
signals.followup: Pull AJPES (SI) and the Hungarian company register (e-cegjegyzek) filings for incorporation dates, registered activity, share capital and directors of the two new entities; watch for Mellon SI/HU hiring adverts on apply.workable.com/mellongroup as the earliest signal of a live sales push.

signals.entity: Camelot Sistemi d.o.o. (Zagreb) - acquired by Mellon Technologies
signals.signal: local-peer. Mellon Technologies acquired 100% of Camelot Sistemi d.o.o., Frankopanska 22, Zagreb (OIB 79572418476, MB 02060582), for an initial consideration of EUR 75,165.60, disclosed in Mellon's 2025 accounts reported 11/08/2026. Croatia's Fina Info.BIZ register confirms Mellon Technologies A.E. as the sole member and Josip Papak as director. Camelot is a micro firm: NKD 62.90 IT services, 1 employee, 2025 total revenue EUR 37,560, EBITDA minus EUR 977, net loss EUR 1,776, share capital EUR 2,650. Its published business is implementation and installation of queue-management systems (QMS - the branch ticketing and customer-flow systems that route walk-in customers to counters) for Swedish manufacturer Nemo-Q.
signals.source_name: Fina Info.BIZ company record, CAMELOT SISTEMI d.o.o., OIB 79572418476 (acquisition disclosed via mononews.gr)
signals.implies: Mellon is buying its way into Croatian branch transformation the same way it won Queue Management across 60+ OTP Banka Srbija branches in February 2026, and it now owns a Nemo-Q QMS delivery capability in Zagreb. That threatens Printec's self-service and bank-kiosk line at Croatian accounts, notably Erste Croatia (an existing Printec OptiCash reference) where a QMS or kiosk foothold is the usual door-opener to the wider self-service estate. Printec Croatia should get ahead of a Mellon QMS pitch by bundling kiosk plus queue-management plus ATM telemetry into its Erste and Zagrebacka conversations.
signals.likelihood: Mellon QMS/branch-kit pitches to Croatian banks within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Check the Croatian court register (sudreg.pravosudje.hr) for the date of the ownership change and any name change to Mellon Croatia; add Camelot Sistemi/Nemo-Q to the competitor roster as a Croatian branch-transformation local-peer.

signals.implies: The Hyosung fleet inside a Ukrainian state bank is serviced by a small local firm rather than any OEM channel, and the same firm also holds Ukrgasbank's Wincor maintenance, a 112-machine NCR SelfServ PC refresh and a 20-ATM NFC retrofit - it is consolidating the whole multivendor service stack at that account. The contract now runs to 31/05/2027, giving Printec's managed and field-services unit a datable re-tender window opening around Q1 2027, and the newly added PCI DSS responsibility matrix is exactly the compliance framing Printec can compete on. signals.entity: Brink's (minority shareholder in KAL ATM Software)
signals.signal: global. Brink's Q2 2026 results, released 05/08/2026, report revenue USD 1.39bn (+7%), 4% organic growth, and ATM Managed Services plus Digital Retail Solutions growing 14% organically - the 14th consecutive quarter of mid-teens-or-better AMS/DRS organic growth, with AMS/DRS now roughly 30-32% of total revenue. Named Q2 wins include a full ATM outsourcing deal with Bank Mandiri in Indonesia and a 5,000-location North American retail DRS agreement. ATMaaS (ATM-as-a-Service) means the bank hands its entire ATM estate - hardware, software, cash replenishment, monitoring and field repair - to one provider for a per-machine fee. Brink's has held a minority stake in KAL since 23/06/2025 and states its AMS offer is deliberately hardware-independent, which is precisely what KAL's multivendor software enables. [STANDING - dated 12/06/2025] Brink's-KAL ATMaaS is still validated only in Asia, the UK and the Middle East, with no named Printec-footprint bank.
signals.implies: The single biggest structural threat to Printec's ATM business is a bank deciding to outsource the whole estate rather than buy hardware, software and services separately - and the company compounding that model at mid-teens growth already operates in Greece, Romania, Czechia and Cyprus. A Brink's AMS win at a footprint bank would displace Printec's NCR hardware, x-core multivendor software, telemetry and field services in one stroke. Printec should package its own end-to-end answer (NCR ATMs plus x-core plus device telemetry plus APTRA OptiCash cash optimisation plus field services) as a single per-ATM managed offer and lead with it at Alpha Bank, BCR, Erste Croatia and Bank of Cyprus before Brink's arrives with a KAL-powered pitch.
signals.likelihood: Continued mid-teens AMS growth through 2027 is near-certain; a first named CEE/SEE AMS logo is plausible within 12 months
signals.followup: Read the Q3 2026 Brink's call for the first named European or CEE AMS logo and for any formal Brink's-KAL joint go-to-market; separately track the Brink's/NCR Atleos merger close, which would put Printec's key OEM partner inside a company that part-owns KAL.

signals.signal: global. A full sweep of KAL's newsroom (all six categories, every article opened for its publication date) found NO new Printec-footprint bank win this run - the most recent post is 02/07/2026, a trade survey whose 2026/27 ATM Software Trends Report is due December 2026. KAL's live commercial pitch is the Windows 11 migration: Microsoft ended mainstream support for non-LTSC Windows 10 on 14/10/2025, and KAL markets Kalignite Hypervisor, a Red Hat-supported Linux virtualisation layer, explicitly so banks can run Windows 11 and later on existing ATMs 'even if unsupported by the ATM hardware vendor' [STANDING - dated 17/09/2025]. Its flagship reference for this is Ceska sporitelna, where the Hypervisor runs on hundreds of ATMs [STANDING - dated 30/05/2024], alongside the full K3A / KTC / KTH suite. Also standing: KAL has extended beyond ATM software into KAL SmartPOS point-of-sale software [STANDING - dated 23/01/2025], KAL SaaS cloud-hosted Kalignite [STANDING - dated 03/02/2025], own hardware (the RTM retail teller machine and the 50kg Cash Capsule ATM), and a zero-licence 'Software-on-Standby' offer that pre-installs Kalignite on a handful of a rival vendor's ATMs so it can be rolled out fleet-wide at will. In the region KAL reaches banks through Asseco Central Europe, whose multivendor ATM application is built on Kalignite and names Slovenska sporitelna and DanubePay.
signals.source_name: KAL ATM Software newsroom and product pages (kal.com)
signals.implies: The Windows 11 ATM migration is the live 2026-27 battleground and KAL's Hypervisor pitch is designed to REMOVE the hardware-refresh trigger that drives Printec's NCR ATM sales - a bank persuaded it can keep its existing machines buys software, not new ATMs. Printec must counter on total cost of ownership: an aged fleet kept alive on a hypervisor still fails mechanically, lacks intelligent-deposit and recycling capability, and cannot carry the deposit-automation revenue that a recycling refresh unlocks. Equally, KAL's Software-on-Standby is a direct wedge under any Printec x-core account - it is cheap for a bank to keep a KAL fallback installed, so Printec should tie x-core renewals to roadmap commitments and Windows 11 certification dates. Watch Asseco Central Europe as KAL's CZ/SK delivery arm in accounts Printec bids.
signals.likelihood: Footprint banks will run Windows 11 ATM migration decisions through 2026-27; KAL/Asseco will be in those conversations in CZ and SK with high likelihood
signals.followup: Ask Printec's NCR channel for x-core's Windows 11 certification status and publish a TCO counter-argument to hypervisor-based fleet life extension; monitor kal.com/en/kal-atm-news and the December 2026 trends report for the first named CEE/SEE Kalignite logo.

signals.entity: Mellon Technologies - Greek POS / Web-ECR acquiring channel
signals.signal: regional. Mellon's Greek POS portal (pos.mellongroup.com) shows its 'ERP Mellon Web-ECR' certification matrix was last updated 27/08/2026 and now lists dozens of Greek ERP and retail-software vendors certified against Mellon's EFT POS / electronic-cash-register interconnection, including Entersoft (Business Suite, Expert, QuickBiz, SmartRetail, SmartPharmaSys), Epsilon CSA (Galaxy, Galaxy Retail, Pylon, Omega, SRS2POS), Pegasus, Orian, NanoSoft, Poseidon Software and many smaller houses, with several marked 'Completed' for both ERP and FIM (fiscal) certification and at least one still 'In progress'. Mellon's portal also documents IRIS instant-payment acceptance over EFT POS and SoftPOS from 01/12/2025, and AADE filings record MELLON TECHNOLOGIES as the provider behind the NBG Pay 'Tap on Mobile' softPOS cash-register interconnection.
signals.source_name: pos.mellongroup.com - 'ERP Mellon Web-ECR' certification matrix (WordPress REST API, page modified date)
signals.implies: Mellon is not only the Hyosung/KAL ATM channel in Greece - it is also building the widest ERP and fiscal-cash-register integration estate around the NBG Pay acquiring stack, which is exactly the lock-in that Worldline/Cardlink built with its All-in-One bundle. Every Greek merchant whose ERP is certified against Mellon's Web-ECR is a merchant Printec's Verifone/Castles POS and TMS proposition has to displace against an integration cost. Printec Greece should publish its own equivalent ERP-certification matrix and target the ERP houses still marked incomplete on Mellon's list.
signals.likelihood: Continued monthly expansion of the certified-ERP list through 2026
signals.followup: Snapshot the certification matrix monthly to track which ERP houses Mellon adds, and cross-check the AADE list of declared-conformity POS models for new Mellon entries.

GENUINE GAPS: no primary registry confirmation of the two new Mellon entities in Slovenia and Hungary (AJPES and the Hungarian register are form/JS-driven - see operator_requests); no ATM or POS unit counts anywhere, which is expected since vendors do not disclose them and none were estimated; no evidence either way on whether the NBG 700-unit Hyosung Series 8 rollout has completed, as neither Mellon nor NBG has published progress; and no named Brink's-KAL ATMaaS customer inside the 17-country footprint.
access_issues: RESOLVED a long-carried block: mellongroup.com/news is JS-rendered with no WordPress or public API, but the page markup exposes a hidden field news_load_url = https://mellongroup.com/news/load. That endpoint returns JSON only when POSTed with the page's csrf_token (harvested from the same page with a cookie jar) plus a page parameter; a bare GET silently returns the OLDEST page, which is why earlier runs concluded there was no API. The full 9-page archive is now readable this way and should be added to the tooling. Also resolved: mellon.hr and mellon.com.pl, previously logged as WAF/redirect blocks, now return valid JSON from /wp-json/wp/v2/posts - both are simply empty (zero posts), so there is no hidden Croatian or Polish Mellon news. STILL BLOCKED: (a) www.kal.com fails TLS verification in the WebFetch tool ('unable to verify the first certificate') - worked around with curl and a desktop User-Agent, which succeeds, so all KAL content in this report was fetched that way; (b) AJPES ePRS (www.ajpes.si/prs) and bizi.si are ASP.NET form/JS registries that return a 404 or an empty shell to a plain fetch, so Mellon Systems and Services d.o.o. Ljubljana could not be confirmed against the Slovenian register; (c) the Hungarian company register (e-cegjegyzek.hu) requires an interactive session, so Mellon Hungary LLC is likewise unconfirmed against a primary registry; (d) prozorro.gov.ua/api/search/tenders rejects GET with 'Method Not Allowed' and needs a POST with a JSON body - documented here so it is not re-discovered; (e) hyosungtns.com (the Korean corporate domain) returned connection code 000 on every attempt, so Hyosung's Korean-language corporate newsroom and any Korean disclosure filings were not reachable - hyosung-tns.com (the global site) was used instead.
